title: Quantitative Analysis of Ginger-Induced Activation of the Cellular Immune System
summary:
Gingerols ([6]-, [8]-, and [10]-gingerol) are natural compounds in ginger that are largely responsible for its characteristic pungency. These compounds activate specific receptors that mediate the perception of pungency. Such receptors are also expressed on cells of the immune system, where they may influence biological processes.
After consuming ginger-containing foods, such as ginger extract, the gingerols enter the bloodstream and are converted into water-soluble metabolites. Laboratory studies and initial human studies have demonstrated measurable effects of gingerol on blood cells. This raised the question of whether such effects can occur even with a realistic and safe dose of ginger extract.
The aim of this study is therefore to investigate whether and to what extent the intake of a ginger and [6]-Gingerol extract causes short-term changes in immune system parameters in the blood. To this end, various blood parameters will be analysed to gain a better understanding of possible biological mechanisms.
In addition, the study will investigate whether interindividual differences in gingerol metabolism are associated with the activity of selected metabolic enzymes and with specific genetic variants, particularly variants of a receptor involved in the perception of pungency.
The study aims to contribute to a better understanding of the potential effects of gingerols on the immune system and their metabolism in the human body.
conditions: Investigation of the immunological response to ginger extract consumption in healthy adults

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m2
Exclusion criteria:
•	Current tobacco use
•	Participation in competitive sports (> 10 hours/week)
•	Known metabolic disorders, such as malabsorption syndromes, lipid metabolism 
        disorders, diabetes mellitus, or untreated thyroid dysfunction
